title: Malcolm-Jamal Warner's Widow Sues Actor's Mother for $1.2 Million in Unfulfilled Prenup Promises
excerpt: Tenisha Warner filed the lawsuit against her mother-in-law on the one-year anniversary of the Cosby Show star's drowning death in Costa Rica, alleging he failed to fund a life insurance policy, retirement account, and salary payments.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Tenisha Warner is suing her mother-in-law for $1.2 million over unfulfilled prenup obligations.
  • The lawsuit claims Malcolm-Jamal Warner failed to secure a $1 million life insurance policy and other financial commitments.
  • The suit was filed on July 20, 2026, marking one year since Warner's drowning death in Costa Rica.
  • Malcolm-Jamal Warner was 54 when he drowned during a family vacation, ruled an accidental death.
  • Tenisha Warner's identity was private until she shared wedding photos months after her husband's death.

  • The alleged unfulfilled promises include a $1 million life insurance policy, a Roth IRA, yearly $16,000 tax-free payments, and a $5,000 monthly salary for Tenisha's work as his assistant

  • Tenisha's identity remained private until she shared wedding photos on social media months after her husband's death

The widow of actor Malcolm-Jamal Warner has filed a lawsuit against his mother over $1.2 million in financial promises she says were left unfulfilled when the beloved television star died last year.

Tenisha Warner filed the suit on July 20, the one-year anniversary of the Cosby Show actor's drowning death in Costa Rica, according to TMZ. The lawsuit names Pamela Warner, Malcolm's mother and the trustee of the Warner Family Trust, as the defendant.

Prenup Promises Never Kept

> **"Local police said the actor was swept up in a strong current at Playa Grande beach in Cahuita, Limon."**

"Local police said the actor was swept up in a strong current at Playa Grande beach in Cahuita, Limon."

According to court documents, Malcolm and Tenisha signed a prenuptial agreement in 2022 that committed the actor to several financial provisions for his wife. These included a $1 million life insurance policy naming Tenisha as the sole beneficiary, funding a Roth IRA, making yearly tax-free payments of $16,000, and paying Tenisha a $5,000 monthly salary for serving as his assistant and chief of staff during their marriage.

Tenisha claims in the filing that Malcolm never purchased or maintained the life insurance policy and did not follow through on the other financial commitments. The suit states the promises went unfulfilled due to his untimely death, according to Page Six.

A Drowning Death in Costa Rica

Tragic Timeline of Events
July 20, 2025
Malcolm-Jamal Warner drowns in Costa Rica.
July 20, 2026
Tenisha Warner files lawsuit against Pamela Warner.

Malcolm-Jamal Warner died on July 20, 2025, at the age of 54, after drowning during a family vacation in Costa Rica. Local police said the actor was swept up in a strong current at Playa Grande beach in Cahuita, Limon. An autopsy by Costa Rica's Forensic Pathology Department ruled the death accidental, caused by asphyxiation by submersion.

Warner was best known for playing Theo Huxtable on The Cosby Show, which aired from 1984 to 1992. He later starred in The Resident and built a career spanning four decades in television, earning three NAACP Image Awards.

A Private Grief Made Public

Tenisha's identity had remained private in the months following her husband's death. She broke her silence on social media several months later, marking their wedding anniversary with never-before-seen wedding photos. The couple shares a daughter whose identity has not been revealed.

Neither Tenisha's legal team nor Pamela Warner has publicly commented on the lawsuit, according to Page Six. The case now moves to the courts, where the question of whether the Warner Family Trust bears responsibility for promises Malcolm made during his lifetime will be decided.
